newsitem.title: UK: UK's Blair to meet top businessmen, wins praise.
newsitem.headline: UK's Blair to meet top businessmen, wins praise.

text.p: Opposition Labour party leader Tony Blair is set to meet top British businessmen on Tuesday night as part of his drive to win over the country's commercial elite ahead of the election which must be held by May.

Aides said Blair would tell top executives from Britain's leading blue-chip companies that the country's business prospects were being harmed by the ruling Conservative party's "open hostility to Europe and talk of withdrawal".

Guests at Tuesday's private dinner, which aides said is one of a series Blair has been holding with business leaders, will include Gerry Robinson, chairman of media company Granada Group Plc, and Duncan Michael, managing partner of Ove Arup.
Aides also released a statement by Michael endorsing Blair, saying: "I am extremely glad that Labour has changed and now works so constructively with business.

"I've been impressed with Tony Blair's understanding of the needs of the business community in this country. His emphasis on better investment in transport and skills and training seems to me absolutely right.
"In addition, he appears to have demonstrated well the leadership the country needs."
Blair's Labour party is 18 to 20 points ahead of the Conservatives with time ticking away to the election.

Prime Minister John Major's ruling party is already in a minority in parliament after a crushing by-election defeat last week. But all the signs are that he intends to hang on until at least May 1 before holding the election.
